english.note: Use this as the all-purpose verb for opening or making something operative, including doors, eyes, valves, shops, accounts, and files.
Use the all-purpose verb 開 for opening something, adding 少少 for opening it slightly and often naming the container for a packaged drink.

examples.english: I open the file to take a look.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 hoi1 zo2 go3 man4 gin6 tai2

examples.english: I crack open the can of soda a little and drink it later.
examples.traditional: 我開少少罐汽水，等陣先飲。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 hoi1 siu2 siu2 gun3 hei3 seoi2 dang2 zan6 sin1 jam2

english.note: Use this colloquial form especially when beginning an event, game, meeting, work session, or other scheduled activity.

examples.english: The meeting will begin at eight.

english.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for starting an app or program.
Use this for switching something on, especially lights, appliances, and devices.
Use this for turning on a device function, feature, or setting, rather than for giving a person the ability to act.

examples.english: I can launch the program with one tap.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 gam6 zau6 hoi1 dou2 go3 cing4 sik1

examples.english: I enable the location feature on my phone.
examples.traditional: 我部手機開咗定位功能。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 bou6 sau2 gei1 hoi1 zo2 ding6 wai6 gung1 nang4
